clue.text: Hansom going into horse, ghastly

indicators.note: the cab is put inside the horse, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a hansom is a horse-drawn cab

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage crashing into its own horse makes a gruesome scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome or ghastly, dwelling on death, is a close synonym.

clue.text: Second mark of approval

definitions.meaning: a very short moment, as in 'just a second'
the check mark put beside a correct answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's second mark of approval on a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British usage: a brief moment, and the check symbol meaning correct.

clue.text: Asian plane diverted over capital in Iran

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the next one
a diverted plane is sent off course, so its letters are sent into a new order
the capital, or first letter, in the word Iran

explanation.surface: An Asian flight is rerouted over the capital of Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' shuffles PLANE into NEPAL, and 'over' puts that above I, the capital letter of Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Nepal is Asian, so the noun is an example of the broader word.

clue.text: Metropolis in saga composed around two hospitals

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, and two of them give two Hs

explanation.surface: A city appears in a saga written about a pair of hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed around' asks for IN SAGA to be rearranged with the two Hs worked in among its letters; the Hs end up separated, so all eight letters are one shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is one of China's largest cities, an example of a metropolis.

clue.text: Knocked sideways, as mouth punched?

parts.note: gob is British slang for the mouth
smacked means hit or punched

explanation.surface: Someone was knocked sideways, like a person punched in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful 'as mouth punched?' reads the British slang word literally: a smacked gob.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for utterly astonished, which the idiom of being knocked sideways also conveys.

clue.text: Stir it into stone

indicators.note: the word it is put into the stone

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: A cook is told to stir something into a stone mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or disturb a liquid, or people, is to shake it about; a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: More than one serviceman remains unreliable

indicators.note: unreliable letters will not stay put, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier's remains are said to be poorly identified.
explanation.definitionFit: Marines are sea-going soldiers, so the plural noun names several servicemen.

clue.text: Yet to admit beer finally finished

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: though can mean yet or however

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of beer

explanation.surface: A pub-goer has yet to confess the beer is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being through with something means it is done or completed, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Wise guy in sting, spy out to trap soldier

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

indicators.note: to trap is to hold inside, so the soldier sits within the other letters
out signals the letters of spy are put out of order

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker of that kind of insect, so ant can stand for soldier

explanation.surface: A know-all is caught in a sting when a spy sets out to trap a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the spy's letters into YPS before the soldier goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a know-it-all, and the British idiom for such a show-off is a synonym.

clue.text: Defender, bit of a pig, in game

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
gammon is cured ham from the hind leg of a pig

explanation.surface: A footballer, part pig, takes part in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two played with dice and counters, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Place in faculty under discussion?

indicators.note: something under discussion is being spoken about, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: sight is one of the faculties or senses

explanation.surface: A query about which place in a university department is being talked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' looks like a university department but is a sense, sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot of ground, a straight synonym for a place.

clue.text: Person calling to restrict a newspaper, more scheming

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the crier holds the other letters

parts.note: a town crier calls out announcements
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A caller tries to limit a newspaper's reach, a rather devious move.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftier is the comparative of crafty, meaning more cunning or wily.

clue.text: Kept in order, drawer showing butterfly

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the drawer sits within the order

parts.note: a friary is the house of a religious order of friars
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: Something kept neatly in a drawer turns out to be a pinned butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests an artist, but it is the cash drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fritillary is a family of orange chequered butterflies, an example of the class.

clue.text: Friendly male interested in painting, say?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
arty describes someone keen on art, painting being one example

explanation.surface: A genial man who likes painting is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty greeting is warm and cordial, so it is a synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Merry king inspired by victories in game

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, or merry

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the king goes inside the victories

parts.note: wins are victories
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tipsy monarch, spurred on by success, plays a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game of flicking small counters into a cup, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Old PM, Democrat from the Middle East

parts.note: an Israeli is from a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is said to be a Democrat of Middle Eastern origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was Britain's prime minister twice in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Nation in trouble, so thoughtless

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A country in difficulty is accused of being so careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by its neighbour, an example of a country.

clue.text: Frozen mass that's large, ice endlessly shifting

indicators.note: shifting letters move about, so they are rearranged
endlessly removes the final letter of ice

explanation.surface: A big frozen mass with ice constantly moving describes a real one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims ICE to IC, which joins LARGE as the letters for 'shifting' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a slow-moving river of ice, a frozen mass of great size.

clue.text: Careless about girl

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone is told they were thoughtless regarding a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means negligent in one's duty, a synonym for careless.

clue.text: Dog shown, bitter

parts.note: aired means broadcast or shown
bitter is a type of British ale

explanation.surface: A dog is exhibited and looks resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Seldom opening in reality, a bank

indicators.note: the opening of reality is its first letter

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A bank rarely shows its true face, opening up to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means not often, a straight adverbial synonym of seldom.

clue.text: End in Indian state, heading for Lucknow

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of Lucknow

explanation.surface: A trip ending in an Indian state, then on towards Lucknow.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or end one works towards, as in 'to that end'.

clue.text: Dessert wine getting another little shake?

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding or dessert
hock is a British name for German white wine

explanation.surface: A diner has pudding with wine and then starts to tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor following an earthquake is a further small shake, so the definition is a playful description.

clue.text: Goddess has essentially brought enlightenment, primarily

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A goddess is said to have brought understanding to humans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' looks like a middle-letter signal, but it is just one of the words whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek deity of youth, cupbearer to the gods, an example of a goddess.

clue.text: Tricky grasping instrument suddenly

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the instrument goes within

parts.note: sly means cunning or tricky
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A cunning, greedy musician produces a sudden note.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that turns sharply does so abruptly, so the adverb is a synonym for suddenly.

clue.text: Sob loudly, seeing whaler's product

definitions.meaning: to cry noisily and without restraint
the fat of a whale, rendered by whalers for oil

explanation.surface: A whaler weeps at the sight of what the hunt produced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to weep noisily and the noun for whale fat.
